A.explanation: Electron, neutrino and positron are all leptons and are not made of quarks.

B.explanation: Proton is a hadron made of quarks, so it is not a lepton even though electron and neutrino are leptons.

C.explanation: Proton and neutron are both hadrons made of quarks, so only the electron in this list is a lepton.

D.explanation: Neutron is a hadron made of quarks, so it is not a lepton even though neutrino and positron are leptons.

walkthrough: List the particles named: electron, neutrino, positron, proton, neutron.
State the rule: leptons are fundamental particles that are not hadrons, and include electrons, neutrinos and their antiparticles such as positrons.
State the contrast: protons and neutrons are hadrons because each is made of three quarks.
Test each list for any hadron: any list containing proton or neutron contains a non-lepton.
Only the list electron, neutrino, positron has no proton and no neutron, so all three are leptons. This is option A.
